bands.1:
You have won the Architect's badge. Now she is on your side.

"The plan has three parts," she says. "First, we climb. Second, we find Maxx's plans. Third, we free Girderoo. In conclusion, wear warm socks."

Indi's disguises are orange vests. The hard hats are saucepans. Mo's is a colander.

Gus holds up a jar of white flakes. "The Dandruff Blizzard! Two years of my dandruff. That's not gross. That's science."

At midnight, you all climb.

A gold drone swings round the tower. Gus shakes the jar. Now its camera sees only snow.

"Why did the blueprint go to the doctor?" asks Mo. "It felt blue!"

Even the wind groans.

At the top is Maxx World. It is not a sanctuary. It is rows of tiny gold cages.

Zed tries MAXXISGREAT on the office door. Beep. Wrong. He types MAXXTERPIECE. The door opens.

The blueprints show a theme park made of cages. One booth says, "SELFIE WITH A SAD CREATURE: $50."

At the gate is a giant statue of Maxx.

"He always draws himself taller," says Wren.

"This park has a way in," says the Architect. "It has no way out. In conclusion, it's a prison."

You roll up the blueprints. That's the proof.

Wren opens the cages. Girderoo jumps into the Architect's arms.

Then Goldies climb up every ladder.

"The Reef Rays are only losing by seventy!" whispers Tully.

"TULLY!"

"Always build a way out," says the Architect.

Girderoo thumps one plank. Every ladder folds flat into a giant slide. The Goldies whoosh down into the snow.

On the boat, you open the last blueprint. In the middle of Maxx World is a tank as big as a lake. It says, "THE BIG ONE. Catch her live!"

"Only one Creature is that big," says the Architect. "Old Glimmer. Nobody has seen her for fifty years."
bands.2:
You have won the Architect's badge, and now she is on your side.

"The plan has three parts," she says. "First, we climb the tower while the Goldies sleep. Second, we find Maxx's plans. Third, we free Girderoo. In conclusion, wear warm socks."

Indi hands out disguises: orange vests that say "TOTALLY REAL BUILDERS" and hard hats that are really saucepans. Mo's hard hat is a colander.

Gus holds up a jar of white flakes. "The Dandruff Blizzard. Two whole years of my dandruff. That's not gross. That's science."

At midnight, the crew starts to climb. The ladders are icy.

A MaxxCam drone swings round the tower. Gus shakes the jar. A thick white flurry swirls into its lens, and the drone films nothing but snow.

"Why did the blueprint go to the doctor?" puffs Mo. "It was feeling blue!"

Even the wind seems to groan.

At the top is Maxx World. It is not a sanctuary. Rows of tiny gold cages stand in the snow, each with a sign that says "HAPPY HOME".

Zed types MAXXISGREAT into the office keypad. It buzzes. Wrong. He types MAXXTERPIECE. The door slides open.

Inside, the blueprints are pinned to the wall. They show a theme park made entirely of cages. Beside the gate is a booth: "SELFIE WITH A SAD CREATURE: $50. SADDER CREATURE: $80."

At the front stands a statue of Maxx, taller than the tower.

"He always draws himself taller," says Wren.

"This does not hang together," says the Architect. "A sanctuary has a way in and a way out. This one has no exit. In conclusion, it's a prison with a gift shop."

You roll up the blueprints. That's the proof.

Behind the office, Wren and the Architect open the cages: Tracewhisks, Topsittles and shivering Stagglets. In the last cage is Girderoo, under a sign that says "MASCOT. PRACTISE SMILING." He leaps into the Architect's arms.

Then floodlights blaze. Goldies swarm up every ladder.

"The Reef Rays are only losing by seventy," whispers Tully. "That's nearly a draw."

"TULLY!"

"First rule of building," says the Architect. "Always build a way out."

Girderoo thumps one plank with his foot. Every ladder below folds flat into a giant slide. The Goldies whoosh down it, straight into a snowdrift.

On the Soggy Biscuit, you unroll the last blueprint. In the middle of Maxx World is a tank as wide as a lake. In gold pen, it says: "STAR ATTRACTION: THE BIG ONE. Catch her live!"

The Architect goes very quiet. "Only one Creature is that big," she says. "Old Glimmer. Nobody has seen her for fifty years."
bands.3:
You have won the Architect's badge, and the builder of Scaffold Peaks is finally on your side. She unrolls a fresh blueprint across Mo's kitchen bench, right on top of the porridge.

"The plan has three parts," she says. "First, we climb the north tower while the Goldies sleep. Second, we find Maxx's plans. Third, we free Girderoo and every Creature with him. In conclusion, wear warm socks."

Indi hands out disguises: orange vests that say "TOTALLY REAL BUILDERS" and hard hats that are really saucepans turned upside down. Mo's hard hat is a colander. "For air flow," says Indi.

Gus holds up a jar of white flakes. "The Dandruff Blizzard," he whispers proudly. "Two whole years of my dandruff. That's not gross. That's science."

At midnight, the crew starts to climb. The ladders are icy, and the wind howls between the towers.

Halfway up, a MaxxCam drone swings round the tower. Gus shakes the jar. A thick white flurry swirls into its lens, and the drone hovers there, filming the most boring snowstorm in history.

"Why did the blueprint go to the doctor?" puffs Mo. "It was feeling blue!"

Even the wind seems to groan.

At the top, behind the gold fence, Maxx World is half built, and it is not a sanctuary. Rows of tiny gold cages stand in the snow, each with a sign that says "HAPPY HOME".

Zed types MAXXISGREAT into the site office keypad. It buzzes angrily. He thinks for a moment, then types MAXXTERPIECE. The door slides open.

Pinned to the wall inside are the blueprints. They show a theme park made entirely of cages. There's a "Cage Coaster" that rattles past the Creatures, and beside the gate is a booth: "SELFIE WITH A SAD CREATURE: $50. SADDER CREATURE: $80."

At the front of it all stands a statue of Maxx, taller than the tower itself.

"He always draws himself taller," says Wren quietly.

The Architect traces the plan with her finger. "This does not hang together. First, a sanctuary needs an entrance. Second, it needs an exit. This one has no exit at all." Her voice goes tight. "In conclusion, it's a prison with a gift shop."

You roll up the blueprints and slip them into your jacket. That's the proof.

Behind the office, Creatures huddle in the cages: Tracewhisks, Topsittles and a jar of shivering Stagglets. In the last cage sits Girderoo, his hard hat crooked, under a sign that says "MASCOT. PRACTISE SMILING."

Wren and the Architect open the cages one by one. Girderoo bounds straight into the Architect's arms.

Then floodlights blaze across the site. Goldies swarm up every ladder.

In Tully's pocket, the radio crackles. "The Reef Rays are only losing by seventy," she whispers. "That's nearly a draw."

"TULLY!"

"First rule of building," says the Architect calmly. "Always build a way out."

Girderoo hops onto the scaffold and thumps one plank with his foot. With a long clatter, every ladder below folds flat into a giant slide. The Goldies whoosh down it, into a deep snowdrift.

The crew slides down after them, Creatures in their arms, laughing all the way to the boat.

Back on the Soggy Biscuit, you unroll the very last blueprint. In the centre of Maxx World is a tank as wide as a lake, labelled in gold pen: "STAR ATTRACTION: THE BIG ONE. Catch her live on opening night!"

The Architect measures it twice. Then she goes very quiet.

"Only one Creature in the world is that big," she says. "Old Glimmer. Nobody has seen her for fifty years."
bands.4:
You have won the Architect's badge, and the builder of Scaffold Peaks is finally on your side. She unrolls a fresh blueprint across Mo's kitchen bench, right on top of the porridge, and pins down the corners with four of his worst muffins.

"The plan has three parts," she says. "First, we climb the north tower while the Goldies sleep. Second, we find Maxx's plans. Third, we free Girderoo and every Creature with him. In conclusion, wear warm socks."

"A speedrun with a proper map," says Zed. "I love it already."

Indi hands out disguises: orange vests made from old life jackets, each one labelled "TOTALLY REAL BUILDERS", and hard hats that are really saucepans turned upside down. Mo's hard hat is a colander. "For air flow," says Indi, avoiding his eyes.

Gus holds up a jar of white flakes. "The Dandruff Blizzard," he whispers proudly. "Two whole years of my own dandruff. That's not gross. That's science. One good shake, and the drones see nothing but snow."

At midnight, the crew starts to climb. The ladders are slick with ice, and the wind howls between the towers like a pack of dingoes. Tully refuses to look down.

"Statistically," she whispers, "a dropped saucepan falls at..."

"Don't," says everyone.

Halfway up, a MaxxCam drone swings round the tower, its red light blinking. Gus shakes the jar. A thick white flurry swirls straight into its lens, and the drone hovers there, faithfully filming the most boring snowstorm in history.

"Why did the blueprint go to the doctor?" pants Mo, hauling himself up another rung. "It was feeling blue!"

Even the wind seems to groan.

At the top, behind the gold fence, Maxx World is half built, and it is not a sanctuary. Rows of tiny gold cages stand in the snow, each with a cheerful sign that says "HAPPY HOME".

The site office is a gold shipping container. Zed types MAXXISGREAT into the keypad, and it buzzes angrily. He thinks for a moment, then types MAXXTERPIECE. The door slides open.

Pinned to the wall inside are the blueprints. Indi lifts her torch. The plans show a theme park made entirely of cages. There's a "Cage Coaster" that rattles past the Creatures, a gift shop selling plush Maxxes, and beside the gate, a booth labelled "SELFIE WITH A SAD CREATURE: $50. SADDER CREATURE: $80."

At the front of it all stands a statue of Maxx, taller than the tower itself.

"He always draws himself taller," says Wren quietly.

The Architect traces the plan with one finger. "This does not hang together," she says. "First, a sanctuary needs an entrance. Second, it needs an exit. This one has no exit at all." Her voice goes tight. "In conclusion, it's a prison with a gift shop."

You roll up the blueprints and slip them inside your jacket. That's the proof.

Behind the office, Creatures huddle in the cages: Tracewhisks, Topsittles, a Heddrake with its tail tucked under its chin, and a jar of shivering Stagglets. In the last cage sits Girderoo, his little hard hat crooked, under a sign that says "MASCOT. PRACTISE SMILING."

Wren and the Architect open the cages one by one. Girderoo bounds straight into the Architect's arms and thumps her chin with his nose.

Then floodlights blaze across the site. Goldies swarm up every ladder at once.

In Tully's pocket, the footy radio crackles. "The Reef Rays are only losing by seventy," she whispers. "That's nearly a draw."

"TULLY!"

"First rule of building," says the Architect calmly. "Always build a way out." She nods at Girderoo.

Girderoo hops onto the scaffold and gives one plank a sharp thump with his foot. With a long, rattling clatter, every ladder below folds flat into a giant wooden slide. The Goldies whoosh down it one after another, yelling all the way, and land in a deep, soft snowdrift.

The crew slides down after them, Creatures cradled in their arms, laughing all the way to the boat.

Back on the Soggy Biscuit, you unroll the very last blueprint. In the centre of Maxx World is an enormous tank, as wide as a lake. Its label is written in gold pen: "STAR ATTRACTION: THE BIG ONE. Catch her live on opening night!"

The Architect measures it twice. Then she goes very quiet.

"Only one Creature in the world is that big," she says. "Old Glimmer. Nobody has seen her for fifty years."
